subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / FinServ AI
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kai Zhang <kai.zhang@finserv.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / FinServ AI

Hi Kai — great to meet today, and thanks for walking us through FinServ AI's inference footprint. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment:

Recap:
- FinServ AI is leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with VPC connectivity for production.
- Primary workload: real-time policy and customer support assistant. Expect bursty traffic with predictable daily peaks.

Open items for sizing (can you confirm these?):
1) Peak TPS target (requests per second) during your busiest 1-hour window
2) Expected sustained TPS (average over a day)
3) Concurrency per request (how many simultaneous user sessions do you expect per model instance)
4) Token mix: % of short (<128 tokens), medium (128-512), long (512-2048+) and typical prompt vs response lengths
5) Model family you want to run in Dedicated (we support variants; include model name/version)
6) Any strict latency SLOs (p95 or p99 targets) and preferred GPU types (A100-80GB, H100, etc.)

I've attached a quick sizing template (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) that you can fill — it helps us map TPS/latency to GPU counts and expected concurrency.

Next steps:
- Kai: can you fill out the template and attach a sample day-of traffic CSV if possible (even a 1-week sample helps).
- Rafael/Aditya: once Kai shares, we'll run a sizing pass and propose two configurations (cost-optimized and latency-optimized) and provide estimated monthly cost and lead time.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx

From: Kai Zhang <kai.zhang@finserv.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / FinServ AI

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. I filled out the sizing template and attached a sample export of last week's traffic (finserv-usage-sample.csv). Answers below inline:

1) Peak TPS (1-hour peak): ~55 TPS (observed during US market open spikes)
2) Sustained TPS (daily average): ~12-18 TPS
3) Concurrency: typical session concurrency ~8-12; occasionally up to 20 for internal batch runs
4) Token mix: ~70% short (<128 tokens), 25% medium (128-512), 5% long (512-2048). Typical prompt+response token size averages ~220 tokens.
5) Model: we're evaluating an open model for now (instruction-tuned 4k context); aim to try both a 16k variant later. For now please size for a 4k model with KV-cache behavior consistent with causal decoder models.
6) Latency SLO: aim for p95 < 300ms for short requests, p95 < 600ms for medium.
7) Preferred GPU: procurement prefers A100-80GB but open to H100 if you recommend for better throughput.

Also: we're leaning Dedicated + VPC (we need data isolation) rather than hosted public API. Procurement will want a cost estimate and lead time for procurement approval.

Attachments: finserv-usage-sample.csv, completed-sizing-template.xlsx

Thanks,
Kai Zhang
Head of ML Platform
FinServ AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kai Zhang <kai.zhang@finserv.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 27 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up / FinServ AI

Hi Kai — this is perfect, thanks for the details and the sample CSV — very helpful. High-level guidance based on your mix and SLOs:

- For your peak (55 TPS) and target p95 latencies, an A100-80GB Dedicated pool is feasible. Recommendation: start with a 6x A100-80GB pool with continuous batching and KV caching enabled (we can tune batch windows for short requests). That configuration targets ~60-70 TPS sustained with the token mix you provided while keeping p95 for short requests near your 300ms target (depends on batching tradeoffs).

- If you prioritize lower latency at peak and plan to expand to the 16k model later, consider 4x H100 (if available) or 8x A100. H100s give better single-request throughput for larger context lengths but may increase cost. We'll provide a cost/throughput comparison in the sizing doc.

- Concurrency: we will size for 12 simultaneous sessions per model shard (headroom for bursts). If you occasionally hit 20 concurrent internal runs, we recommend configuring an autoscale burst policy to add capacity during scheduled batch windows.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Rafael/Aditya: can you run the sizing calc and produce two proposals: (A) cost-optimized (6x A100-80GB) and (B) latency/scale-optimized (4x H100 or 8x A100) with monthly cost, expected p95/p99 estimates, and lead time.
2) Kai: share procurement timeline and any Po or contract templates; we'll include expected lead times in the proposals (include DocuSign link when ready).
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review proposals.

I'll attach the initial rough calc and a short note on caching/batching knobs.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-sample-calc.pdf
